selected.rationale: Home-timeline write fanout is the heaviest synchronous dependency of compose-post; introducing delay causes unbounded latency propagation and can exhaust compose-post threads due to missing timeouts.
Post-storage is the central write/read backend; delaying it stalls every compose request and also impacts home-timeline reads, exposing absent timeout/retry defenses.
Unique-id is the first mandatory call in compose-post; a delay blocks all post creation requests and demonstrates unbounded latency propagation without a client timeout.
Home-timeline service synchronously fetches social graph data on read; a delay hangs timeline loading because there is no timeout on this call.
User-timeline write is a synchronous fan-out in the post path; delay propagates directly to compose-post and can cause availability degradation.
Killing post-storage takes down both compose-post writes and home-timeline reads, exposing the lack of graceful degradation or failover.
A single lost write to post-storage causes the entire post creation to fail if there is no retry, and may leave other fan-out writes in an inconsistent state.
Home-timeline service is used by both write fan-out and read timeline requests; its failure makes multiple endpoints unavailable and shows no recovery fallback.
Timeline reads depend on post-storage; delaying this edge produces user-facing hangs, confirming missing timeout on the read path.
Loss of the unique-id response without retry prevents all post creation, confirming the lack of retry/fallback for a critical dependency.
